candidates: In Vitest test files in this codebase, always use the `{ spy: true }` option in `vi.mock()` calls, move all mock behavior implementations into `beforeEach` blocks, and access mocks via `vi.mocked()` for type safety. Never place inline `vi.fn()` or `mockImplementation()` calls directly inside `vi.mock()` factory functions.

When writing type guards or predicates that detect Vitest project-list array properties in the AST (e.g., `isProjectsArrayProp`), check for both `projects` and `workspace` key names—`workspace` is the deprecated Vitest 3.0–3.1 spelling and `projects` is the 3.2+ spelling. Matching only one name causes the other shape to fall through to incorrect handling.

When resolving named variable declarations from a Babel AST (`ast.program.body`), always check both bare `VariableDeclaration` nodes and `VariableDeclaration` nodes wrapped inside `ExportNamedDeclaration` nodes (i.e., `export const foo = ...`). Omitting the `ExportNamedDeclaration` case silently fails for exported variables. The dual-check pattern is already established in `findVarInitialization.ts` and `ConfigFile.ts` and should be replicated wherever variable initialization is looked up.

When choosing between template variants based on the content of an existing config file (e.g., detecting whether the config uses `workspace` vs. `projects`), resolve the exported config value through the same AST export-resolution path used by the main config-update logic, rather than scanning the raw file text. A raw scan misses variable-exported or aliased config shapes (e.g., `const test = { workspace: [...] }; export default defineConfig({ test })`) and can false-positive on unrelated nested objects.

When writing unit tests for template-based config transforms, apply the same preprocessing steps that the production code performs on the template (e.g., stripping placeholder tokens, removing empty entries) before passing the result to the parser. Using the raw `loadTemplate()` output produces snapshots that don't match the real code path and can hide regressions in the preprocessing step.

Ensure every test case within a `describe` block has a unique, descriptive name. Duplicate test names make failures ambiguous and suggest the scenario is being tested twice; remove the duplicate or rename it to reflect the distinct behavior it actually covers.

When maintaining an allowlist of config properties that must remain at the top level rather than being moved into project entries (e.g., `coverage`), prefer deriving the list from the TypeScript types exported by the library being wrapped (e.g., Vitest's own types) rather than maintaining a hand-written list. This ensures future library versions that introduce new top-level-only properties are caught at compile time instead of causing silent mis-migration.
